_comment: Ground truth for the live checks. Every line is a case whose answer is known from the real world, not from this tool. Run with `nameproof doctor`. A check that cannot reproduce these has drifted, and drift here is silent: every bug this file exists to catch returned a confident, plausible, wrong answer rather than crashing.

name: drata
why: A real company that owns its suggestion list: drata login, drata glassdoor, drata trust center, drata ipo. The Pokemon dratini sits at position 4 and loses. This is what a healthy launched brand looks like, and it is the only positive control in the file.

name: vanta
why: A very large funded company that still does NOT own its name: vantage, vantage west, vantablack, vantaca. Proves the finding is a cost rather than a veto, and that company size does not decide it. If this ever comes back clean the threshold has been loosened too far.

name: wedpalette
why: The case the module was built for. A real site whose entire search demand is redirected: every suggestion is web palette or weed palette. Available, phonetically fine, and invisible.

name: normfin
why: Caught the substring bug. normfin IS a substring of normfinder, so a naive `in` test called it clean while Google offered normfinder, normfinder qpcr, norm finkelstein. A longer word starting with your name is the case that hurts most and the one a substring test always misses.

name: normix
why: Caught the inverted reading. Comes back at 14 of 15 keeping the spelling, which looked like health, because normix medication and normix 200 mg are an ANTIBIOTIC owning the string. For an unlaunched name a high ratio means somebody else got there first.

name: tutify
why: Same inversion, different owner: tutify login, tutify academy, tutify math is a tutoring service. Kept as a second case because one example of an inverted reading is an anecdote.

name: probero
why: Hijacked by a fishing tackle brand: proberos reel, proberos lures, proberos fishing line. This tool recommended it before the whole-word fix landed.

name: anchor
why: An ordinary English word. Google's own Site names guidance says a generic name is unlikely to be selected as a site name unless the brand is already very well known, which is a loop a new company starts inside.

name: vanta
why: A coined word. Guards the opposite direction: a dictionary check that fires on everything is the same as no check at all.

name: anchor
why: Wikidata returns the mooring device, the heraldic figure, an Illinois village, and the podcast platform now called Spotify for Creators. Four different things a searcher could mean.

name: google.com
why: Positive control for RDAP. If this ever reports free, the registry path is broken and every availability answer in the tool is worthless.

name: qzxkwvbnmplzz-test-4471.com
why: Negative control. A 404 from the registry has to keep meaning free; if this reports taken or unknown, the client is being throttled or blocked and the whole batch is suspect.

name: Analfin
why: The offline gate, positive control. A coined name carrying an unambiguous fragment has no other reading available, so this is what its search results are about. Dylan, 2026-08-25, on hitting one of these for real: 'ca c'etait vraiment un no go'.

name: Analytics
why: The Scunthorpe control, and the reason the gate is trustworthy. An ordinary English word carries its own meaning and the fragment inside it is a coincidence of spelling. A gate that blocks this is a gate somebody disables within a week.

name: Cultura
why: The SOFT tier must never block. 'cul' is obscene in French and also sits inside culture, calculus and Oculus, a real and successful brand. This case fails the moment a productive fragment is promoted into the hard list.

name: creampie
why: The online half, positive control. Wiktionary labels it pornography, vulgar, slang. Google's suggest endpoint returns ZERO suggestions for this word, identical to a clean fresh coinage, which is precisely why the search check cannot be the gate and this one has to exist.

name: stripe
why: The negative control that sets the trigger set, and it is not hypothetical: Stripe is one of the most successful company names in software, and Wiktionary labels it slang among others. A check that fired on the bare 'slang' label would have rejected it. Only sexual and abusive labels trigger.

name: msbreewc
why: The case that created this check, and the only one whose evidence is a screenshot. Dylan searched a real candidate, msbrenew, and Google's results page corrected it to this string: an adult creator with over a million followers, Pornhub first. Read directly, onlyfans.com sits fourth on both Bing and DuckDuckGo. Positive control for reading actual results instead of guessing at them.

name: msbrenew
why: The negative control AND the honest boundary of this check. The candidate itself comes back clean on both readable engines (fincen.gov, fintrac-canafe.canada.ca, msrenewal.com), because Bing and DuckDuckGo read it as MSB renewal. Only Google rewrites it into the name above, and Google answers 429 with a captcha even to a stealth browser. Verified through a real browser on 2026-08-25 with gl=us&hl=en&pws=0&safe=off: Google answers 'These are results for msbreewc' and returns Pornhub, OnlyFans, xHamster, Fansly and XVideos in the first ten, so the rewrite is not a Spanish-locale artifact. If this case ever flags, an engine started correcting like Google and the boundary documented in serp.py has moved.
